title: Traktor
description: Anskaffelsens formål er å anskaffe en traktor til kommunal drift, inkludert vintervedlikehold (brøyting/strøing), transport og generelle vedlikeholdsoppgaver. Maskinen skal være egnet for helårsbruk og høy belastning. Anskaffelsen er en engangsanskaffelse, med medfølgende service- og vedlikeholdsavtale. Det vil være anledning til å oppgi en samarbeidspartner for service og vedlikehold. Anskaffelsen omfatter også en opsjon på innbytte av dagens traktor. For ytterligere informasjon om anskaffelsens innhold vises det til del 2 bilag 1 Oppdragsgivers krav og funksjonsbeskrivelse.

title: Kvalifisering- Rammeavtale av helikoptertjenester for Kjøpekraft Vest
description: Anskaffelsen gjelder rammeavtale for leveranser av helikoptertjenester.Helikoptertjenestene ønskes utført i 4 geografiske områder; Hordaland (sør for Sognefjorden), Rogaland, Sogn og Fjordane (nord for Sognefjorden), og Møre og Romsdal. Det presiseres at disse områdene angir oppdragsgivers primære behov, men at det i kontraktsperioden også kan oppstå behov for tilsvarende tjenester i øvrige deler av Vestlandet. Oppdragsgiver har til hensikt å inngå kontrakter med inntil fire (4) leverandører per geografiske område, og forbeholder seg retten til å inngå kontrakter med færre leverandører dersom det ikke foreligger et tilstrekkelig antall tilbud som oppfyller konkurransens krav og vilkår.Volumfordelingen mellom områdene kan variere.Det antas at de fleste oppdrag kan utføres med lite/mellomstort helikopter.Kjøpekraft Vest er ikke kjent med per i dag om oppdrag som krever stort helikopter (+ 3000 kg), men det tas forbehold om at det kan oppstå akutte hendelser/situasjoner hvor det kan være behov for det.Uforutsette oppgaver vil i stor grad være assistanse ved ulike driftssituasjoner bl.a. ved feil på kraftanlegg og ledninger. For å sikre at helikopter i størst mulig grad er tilgjengelig i slike situasjoner er det et krav at helikopterselskapet har tilgjengelige helikoptre på Vestlandet. Det innebærer at ved akutte behov/hendelser vil det bli krevd at et helikopter skal møte etter avtalt tid.Oppdragsgiver presiserer at den planlagte virksomheten for kommende sesonger er beheftet med usikkerhet, og at oppgitt estimert kontraktsverdi i punkt 1.3 er basert på historiske verdier. Det må i tillegg påregnes at det kan bli behov for flyging knyttet til uforutsette oppgaver utover planlagt aktivitet.Dette er kvalifiseringsfasen av konkurransen.

Avtalen omfatter volumlisensavtaler og retter seg mot forhandlerleddet. Rammeavtale formål er kjøp av lisenser, forvaltning og rådgivning på lisensavtaler med stort volum til oppdragsgiver sine medlemskommuner. Avtalen omfatter volumlisensavtaler/volumiering (LAR- status). Leverandøren må og tilby lisensforvaltningsportal. Oppdragsgiver vil vektlegge at leverandøren i tillegg kan tilby service og support m.m. i avtaleperioden. Det vil være et krav til leverandøren at det blir levert gode tjenester til enhver tid. Formålet med anskaffelsen er å redusere innkjøpskostnadene, forenkle anskaffelser av lisenser, samt sikre en god administrasjon av disse.

title: Norway – Air transport services – Qualification - Framework agreement for helicopter services for Purchasing power West
description: The procurement is for a framework agreement for the delivery of helicopter services. The helicopter services are requested to be carried out in 4 geographical areas; Hordaland (south of Sognefjorden), Rogaland, Sogn og Fjordane (north of Sognefjorden), and Møre og Romsdal. Emphasis is put on the fact that these areas state the contracting authority ́s primary need, but that in the contract period there can also be a need for equivalent services in other parts of Western Norway. The contracting authority intends to enter into contracts with up to four (4) tenderers per geographical area and reserves the right to enter into contracts with fewer tenderers if there is not a sufficient number of tenders that fulfil the competition ́s requirements and terms. The volume distribution between the areas can vary. Most of the assignments are expected to be carried out with small/medium sized helicopters. Purchasing power West is not currently aware of assignments that require a large helicopter (+ 3,000 kg), but it is subject to acute incidents/situations where needed. Unforeseen assignments will mostly be assistance in various operational situations, including errors in power installations and pipelines. In order to ensure that the helicopter is as accessible as possible in such situations, it is a requirement that the helicopter company has available helicopters in Western Norway. This means that in the event of acute needs/events, a helicopter will be required to meet at the agreed time. The contracting authority emphasises that the planned entity for the coming seasons is subject to uncertainty and that the stated estimated contract value in point 1.3 is based on historical values. In addition it must be expected that there may be a need for flights connected to unforeseen assignments beyond the planned activity. This is the qualification phase of the competition.

title: Copenhagen - New Metroline, M5 Civil Works South
description: This tender presents a substantial opportunity for prospective contractors to bid for the M5 Civil Works South (CWS) package, an important component of the Copenhagen metro system's expansion. This project is of significant strategic importance, as the M5 line is a fully automated driverless metro system that will not only enhance passenger service on existing metro corridors but also extend connectivity to emerging urban development areas, including Kløverparken, Refshaleøen, and Lynetteholm in the East Harbour. The M5 is designed to operate as an independent system, ensuring that its construction and subsequent operation do not disrupt the existing M1-M4 metro lines. MAIN COMPONENTS OF THE M5 CIVIL WORK The M5 south consists of approx 6.5 km twin bored TBM tunnels, 5 underground stations (incl. 3 transfer stations), 2 underground crossovers, 1 shaft, 5 cross passages, 1 ramp, approx 2.0 km viaduct, 1 elevated station, 1 viaduct cross-over, 1 elevated bifurcation, short embankment sections. For further details on scope ref. is made to M5-2.1-CMBS-SW and M5-2.2-CWS-SW PHASES: The current tender, Phase 1, encompasses the southern section of the line, from north-west of København H to north of v/Prags Boulevard, with an anticipated operational commencement in 2036. The broader vision includes phase 2 north of v/Prags Boulevard to Lynetteholm opening in 2045 and a potential future extension to form a ring line, signifying a long-term commitment to urban mobility. Phase 2 is not included in this tender. CONTRACT SPLIT OF M5: The M5 project as a whole consists of several contracts: • M5 Civil Works South (this contract) • M5 Transportation System South contract (tendered out as a separate contract in June 2026) • Operation and Maintenance contract (will be tendered out at a later stage) • Enabling Works contracts, e.g. relocation of utilities, relocation works at Kh etc. (enabling works will be tendered out in separate contracts) • Station and Shaft areas (will be tendered out at a later stage) • Canopy contracts (will be tendered out at a later stage). CONTRACT The contract is structured as a design & build contract under ABT18 terms, placing comprehensive responsibility for both design and execution upon the Contractor. This two-phase approach—design followed by execution—is a standard framework for complex infrastructure projects. A market dialogue has been carried out before issuing the tender. The purpose of the market dialogue was to ensure that the project is attractive to the market, and to ensure competitive and compliant final tenders to be used as basis for the award of contract. Metroselskabet I/S is grateful for the potential tenderers who took their time to participate in the dialogue and provided input. INDICATIVE TIMESCHEDULE FOR THE PROCUREMENT Publication of contract notice September 10th 2026. Publication of tender documentation September 11th 2026. Deadline for submission of application for prequalification October 13th 2026, ref. made to section 5.1.12. Dialogue phase November 2026-October 2027. Final tender November 2027. Award of contract December 2027. The time-schedule may be subject to change.

title: Belgium – Event services – Raamovereenkomst externe cateringpartners maatwerk en evenementen
description: Voorwerp van deze diensten: Raamovereenkomst externe cateringpartners maatwerk en evenementen Toelichting: Hogeschool VIVES Zuid en VIVES Noord organiseert jaarlijks een brede waaier aan evenementen en “High-end” maatwerkopdrachten binnen zowel de campussen Noord als Zuid, die zich verspreid bevinden in de provincie West-Vlaanderen. Deze activiteiten maken integraal deel uit van het academisch en maatschappelijk functioneren van de hogeschool en vragen een professionele, kwalitatieve en betrouwbare cateringondersteuning. De catering speelt hierbij een cruciale rol in de beleving, uitstraling en organisatorische kwaliteit van deze momenten. Fases van de opdracht: 1ste fase – Selectie Onderhavig document betreft de eerste fase, met name de selectiefase, van een plaatsingsprocedure in twee stappen. In deze eerste fase wordt enkel een “Aanvraag tot deelneming” gevraagd, aangevuld met de nodige bijlagen, waarmee de kandidaat zijn interesse voor de opdracht betoont, zijn schriftelijke wil uit om geselecteerd te worden (artikel 2, 12° Wet Overheidsopdrachten 17 juni 2016) en de gevraagde verantwoordingsstukken overmaakt teneinde geselecteerd te kunnen worden. 2de fase - Gunning Na de selectie kunnen enkel de geselecteerde kandidaten deelnemen aan de tweede fase, de gunningsfase, op basis van het bestek dat hen zal worden bezorgd na de selectiebeslissing. In deze tweede fase zullen de geselecteerde kandidaten op basis van het bestek worden uitgenodigd om een offerte in te dienen. Percelen: - voor perceel 1 “Evenementen” zoeken wij drie externe cateringpartners die de hogeschool gedurende een periode van vier jaar kunnen ondersteunen bij onderstaande activiteiten die flexibel inzetbaar zijn over alle campussen heen dus over de gehele provincie West-Vlaanderen kunnen bedienen. Evenementen: Elk academiejaar voorziet Hogeschool VIVES onder andere 3 grootschalige institutionele evenementen waaronder de Academische Opening in september, de Nieuwjaarsreceptie in januari en de Pro-dag in mei; Voor deze evenementen wordt telkens een opkomst verwacht van ongeveer 700 tot 1.000 aanwezigen. Daarnaast organiseert Hogeschool VIVES jaarlijks meerdere proclamaties, promotiezittingen etc. gespreid over de verschillende studiegebieden. Deze plechtigheden vinden plaats per opleiding of groep en richten zich op studenten en hun ouders of begeleiders. Ook voor deze momenten is een aangepaste, verzorgde en vlot georganiseerde catering vereist, rekening houdend met variërende groepsgroottes, locaties en praktische omstandigheden. - voor perceel 2 “maatwerkopdrachten” zoeken wij eveneens drie externe cateringpartners, voor aanzienlijk kleinere opdrachten van gemiddeld 10 tot 50 personen waar een uitzonderlijk hoog kwaliteitsniveau primeert, zowel op vlak van producten, presentatie en service. “High-end” maatwerkopdrachten: Dit perceel heeft betrekking op de levering van hoogwaardige, op maat uitgewerkte cateringdiensten, waarbij de nadruk expliciet ligt op kwaliteit, exclusiviteit en beleving. De aanbestedende overheid beoogt met dit perceel de selectie van dienstverleners die in staat zijn om cateringconcepten te ontwikkelen en te realiseren die volledig afgestemd zijn op de specifieke context, doelstellingen en doelgroep van elk evenement. Het betreft hierbij geen standaardaanbod, maar telkens een unieke invulling waarbij maatwerk centraal staat. Looptijd De raamovereenkomst heeft een initiële looptijd van vier jaar, op voorwaarde dat de geraamde maximale waarde van de opdracht binnen deze termijn niet wordt overschreden. De aanbestedende overheid vestigt de aandacht van de kandidaat op het feit dat de aangegeven maximumwaarde niet is berekend op basis van de vermoedelijke hoeveelheden in de inventaris. Deze maximale waarde biedt dus geen aanwijzing voor het offertebedrag waarvoor de inschrijving kan worden gegund. Het gaat in dit geval over de maximale waarde van de raamovereenkomst, die vastgesteld is op basis van de maximaal te bestellen hoeveelheden over alle opdrachten die de aanbestedende overheid kan plaatsen. Om de omvang van de opdracht te controleren, houdt de aanbestedende overheid toezicht over de uitgaven in kader van de raamovereenkomst om ervoor te zorgen dat zij de maximale waarde van de raamovereenkomst niet overschrijden. Bij overschrijding van de maximale waarde, kunnen er geen nieuwe bestellingen worden geplaatst.

description: Neubau eines Stellwerks auf einem Streckenabschnitt von ca. 7,7 Kilometern einer mit 750 V DC elektrifizierten öffentlichen Eisenbahn (Hauptbahn) zwischen den Bahnhöfen Wesseling Süd und Bornheim-Hersel mit 28 Weicheneinheiten, 10 vorhandenen hauptsignalabhängigen Bahnübergangssicherungsanlagen, Ausrüstung mit Ks-Signalen in LED-Technik, neuer Gleisfreimeldung, Stromversorgung, Kabellieferung und -verlegung, Zugbeeinflussung PZB und magnetischer Fahrsperre, Anpassung der Nachbarstellwerke vom Typ Siemens SICAS ECC und SpDrS60, Einbindung in das vorhandene VICOS-Bediensystem, Projektierung der Zuglenkung, Neubau eines Stellwerksgebäudes, Prüfleistungen, Inbetriebnahme und Abnahmeprüfung. Die gelieferte Stellwerkstechnik muss für den Betrieb bei öffentlichen Eisenbahnen in Deutschland uneingeschränkt zugelassen sein, den anerkannten Regeln der Technik entsprechen und AK 7/SIL 4 erfüllen, Weichen mit beweglichen Herzstückspitzen unterstützen und für den Verkehr mit Stadtbahnfahrzeugen mit von der EBO abweichenden Rädern geeignet sein. Alle Zulassungen müssen zum Zeitpunkt der Angebotsabgabe uneingeschränkt vorliegen. Fertigstellung und Inbetriebnahme sind zwingend im August 2028 erforderlich. Das neue Stellwerk wird in den nächsten Jahren voraussichtlich um einen weiteren Bahnhof in derselben Technik erweitert.

description: Errichtung einer industriellen Aufbereitungsanlage zur Verarbeitung von Grasschnitt und Laub aus der Landschaftspflege zu pelletierten oder brikettierten Festbrennstoffen (Kapazität ca. 3.100 t/a) am Standort Industriegelände 6, 17139 Malchin, im Rahmen des vom BMEL über die FNR geförderten Verbundprojekts MOOReturn. Der Auftrag umfasst als Generalübernehmerleistung: Planung (einschließlich Genehmigungsplanung), Bauleistungen (Ertüchtigung der Bestandshalle inkl. Hallentore, Medienerschließung, brandschutztechnischer Ertüchtigung, Sozial- und Sanitärräume) sowie die Beschaffung und Montage sämtlicher Anlagenkomponenten der Prozesskette (Dosierung, Waschmaschine, Abtropftrommel, Feinzerkleinerung, Pressentwässerung, thermische Trocknung, Verdichtung). Die Vergabe als integrierte Gesamtleistung dient der Vermeidung von Schnittstellenrisiken und der Sicherstellung einer einheitlichen, vom Generalübernehmer verantworteten Anlagenkonformität. Die Umsetzung des Auftrags ist in aufeinander aufbauenden Leistungsstufen vorgesehen. Der Auftraggeber beabsichtigt, einzelne Leistungsstufen entsprechend dem Projektfortschritt abzurufen. Die Beauftragung weiterer Leistungsstufen erfolgt jeweils vorbehaltlich der Bereitstellung der Fördermittel sowie des Erreichens der definierten Projektmeilensteine. Ein Anspruch auf Beauftragung weiterer Leistungsstufen besteht nicht. Ausführliche Beschreibung des Beschaffungsvorhabens s. title: Germany – Load-bearing structure design services – Planungsleistungen Tragwerksplanung gemäß HOAI, Teil 4, Abschnitt 1, §51 für die Maßnahme Neubau/Anbau: Kindergarten Renquishausen
description: Die Gemeinde Renquishausen plant den Neubau eines 4-gruppigen Kindergartens in der Ortsmitte, angrenzend an das Gemeindezentrum. Innerhalb des Gemeindezentrums werden ehemalige Schulräume künftig nicht mehr benötigt und stehen zur Erweiterung der Feuerwehr und für die Nutzung durch den neuen Kindergarten zur Verfügung. Die Verbindung der Bestandsstruktur und Erweiterung soll den Nutzern einen modernen Kindergarten und Synergien mit den bestehenden Nutzungen bieten. Das Grundstück befindet sich in stadträumlich anspruchsvoller Hanglage. Der zweigeschossige Neubau nutzt die Höhenentwicklung für ebenerdige Zugänge in beiden Geschossen. Der Neubau bindet über einen eingeschossen Zwischenbau mit Dachterrasse an die bestehende Gemeindehalle an.

description: Important Note: The closing date for the initial RFSA solicitation period is the date posted on page 1 of the RFSA Document. The closing date posted on the CanadaBuys webpage serves only to allow for ongoing qualification as outlined in section Supply Arrangement under article 3.1 On-going Opportunity for Qualification of the RFSA. Any arrangements received late will not be considered and will need to be resubmitted during the next available qualification period: April and September of each year. This requirement is for the Department of Fisheries and Oceans (DFO). Title: Request for Supply Arrangement – Ghost Gear The Department of Fisheries and Oceans Canada has a requirement to establish Supply Arrangements for crews and vessels capable of retrieving and appropriately disposing of ghost gear in Canadian waters when the need arises. DFO’s retrieval requirement might be different every time ghost gear is reported due to the conditions, location, sensitive habitats and gear type. DFO does not know the specific requirements until the location and gear is observed. • Retrieval activities may include: mapping capacity (ie. Side scan sonar or similar) to identify targets • Retrieval (by various methods including but not limited to: by hand from vessel, commercial diver, remotely operated vehicle (ROV), barge and excavator). • Transportation to disposal location which may require a boat, barge, truck, etc. • Disposal, including recycling when appropriate PERIOD OF THE SUPPLY ARRANGEMENT The resulting Supply Arrangement will have no defined end-date and will remain valid until such time as Canada no longer considers it to be advantageous to use it. SECURITY There is no security requirement for this contract. Suppliers working under this Supply Arrangement must not be given access to sensitive information or assets, and must be escorted at all times while on DFO premises. TRADE AGREEMENTS This requirement is subject to the Canada-Chile Free Trade Agreement (CCFTA), Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), Canada-Colombia Free Trade Agreement, Canada-Peru Free Trade Agreement (CPFTA), Canada-Panama Free Trade Agreement, Canada-Korea Free Trade Agreement (CKFTA), Canada–Ukraine Free Trade Agreement, Canada-Honduras Free Trade Agreement, Canada-United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement, World Trade Organization–Agreement on Government Procurement (WTO-GPA), and the Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA). MANDATORY REQUIREMENTS Arrangements will be evaluated in accordance with the mandatory evaluation criteria as detailed in the Request for Supply Arrangements. Suppliers’ arrangements must clearly demonstrate that they meet all Mandatory Requirements for the proposal to be considered for further evaluation. Arrangements not meeting the mandatory criteria will be excluded from further consideration. Mandatory Criteria M1 The Supplier must have experience in one or more of the following: 1. surveying 2. retrieving ghost gear from in water 3. transporting ghost gear 4. responsibly disposing of ghost gear 4. Returning of identifiable gear IMPORTANT NOTICE on Insurance Requirements: At the Request for Proposal (RFP) stage, the Offeror will be required to provide valid certificates of insurance demonstrating that the insurance coverage applicable to the nature of the work is in place and maintained. COMPREHENSIVE LAND CLAIMS AGREEMENTS This Request for Supply Arrangements (RFSA) is to establish supply arrangements for the delivery of the requirement detailed in the RFSA to the Identified Users across Canada, excluding locations within Yukon, Northwest Territories, Nunavut, Quebec, and Labrador that are subject to Comprehensive Land Claims Agreements (CLCAs). Any requirement for deliveries to locations within CLCAs areas within Yukon, Northwest Territories, Nunavut, Quebec, or Labrador will have to be treated as a separate procurement, outside of the resulting supply arrangements.” SELECTION METHOD – MANDATORY TECHNICAL CRITERIA To be declared responsive, an arrangement must comply with the requirements of the Request for Supply Arrangements and meet all mandatory technical evaluation criteria. Enquiries regarding this Request for Supply Arrangements are to be submitted in writing to the following: Tammy O’Toole Acting Senior Contracting Officer Procurement Services Fisheries and Oceans Canada Email : DFOtenders-soumissionsMPO@dfo-mpo.gc.ca

title: Refrigeration and HVAC Services at the Pacific Biological Station (PBS), Nanaimo, British Columbia (B.C.).
description: BACKGROUND INFORMATION Canada is seeking offers from Offerors to provide refrigeration and HVAC maintenance and repair services to the Pacific Biological Station (PBS) of the Department of Fisheries and Oceans Canada (DFO) located in Nanaimo B.C. Canada intends to issue up to two (2) Standing Offers. Compliant offers will be ranked in ascending order according to their total evaluated price. The compliant offer with the lowest evaluated price will be ranked first, and the compliant offer with the second-lowest evaluated price will be ranked second. Canada may issue fewer than two Standing Offers if fewer than two compliant offers are received. SCOPE OF WORK The Contractor must provide all labour, materials, tools, equipment, supervision, and travel necessary to deliver refrigeration and HVAC maintenance and repair services on an as-and-when-requested basis by means of a Call-up against the Standing Offer at the Pacific Biological Station (PBS), Nanaimo, British Columbia, for the Department of Fisheries and Oceans Canada (DFO). All work must be performed in accordance with the applicable federal and provincial codes, regulations, and standards listed under the References section of this standing offer. Where discrepancies exist between codes, the most stringent requirement applies. A. Services Services required under this standing offer include, but are not limited to: a. Assembling pipe sections, tubing, and fittings using couplings, clamps, screws, bolts, cement, plastic solvent, caulking, soldering, brazing, and welding equipment; b. Filling pipes or HVAC fixtures with water or air and observing pressure gauges to detect and locate leaks; c. Servicing glycol heating and cooling loops; d. Servicing and installing boilers (steam and condensing) and associated equipment; e. Servicing rooftop units, heat pumps, and hydronic heating systems; f. Servicing heat exchangers; g. Reviewing blueprints, building codes, and specifications to determine work details and procedures; h. Preparing written cost estimates for labour and materials prior to commencing work (see Section 7 — Scheduling); i. Studying building plans and inspecting structures to assess material and equipment needs, establish pipe installation sequences, and plan installations around obstructions such as electrical wiring; j. Maintaining records of all assignments and producing detailed work reports; k. Performing calculations and planning for complex or large-scale jobs; l. Locating and marking positions of pipe installations, connections, passage holes, and fixtures using precision measuring instruments including rulers and laser levels; m. Measuring, cutting, threading, and bending pipe to required angles using hand and power tools, including pipe cutters, pipe-threading machines, and pipe-bending machines; n. Installing pipe assemblies, fittings, and valves for all HVAC equipment; o. Cutting openings in structures to accommodate pipes and pipe fittings using hand and power tools; p. Hanging steel supports from ceiling joists (concrete, steel, or wood) to hold pipes in place; q. Repairing and maintaining HVAC equipment, including replacing defective components, mending or replacing broken pipes, and clearing clogged drains; r. Directing workers engaged in pipe cutting, preassembly, and installation of plumbing systems and components; and s. Supplying and installing stainless steel, ABS, and PVC piping, valves, and associated fixtures for HVAC equipment. B. Equipment Equipment covered under this standing offer includes, but is not limited to: • Distribution piping systems: PVC, ABS, steel, stainless steel, copper, cast iron, PEX, and flexible steel-braided; • Water and glycol circulation pumps; • Sump pumps; • Valves: ball, gate, butterfly, globe, pinch, disc check, and equivalent types; • Safety valves associated with the ammonia refrigeration system; • Glycol heating loop equipment; • Boilers: steam and condensing; • Rooftop units, heat pumps, and hydronic heating systems; • Air compressors; • Air dryers; and • Heat exchangers. CALL-UP PROCEDURES – RIGHT OF FIRST REFUSAL 1. Call-up by Authorized Representative. The Identified User’s authorized representative places a Call-up under the Standing Offer for goods, services, or both included in, and at the prices and in accordance with the terms and conditions specified in, the Standing Offer. 2. Multiple Standing Offers. Call-ups will be issued using a right of first refusal basis: The call-up procedures require that when a requirement is identified, the Identified User will contact the highest-ranked offeror to determine if the requirement can be satisfied by that offeror. If the highest-ranked offeror is able to meet the requirement, a call-up is made against its standing offer. If that offeror is unable to meet the requirement, the identified user will contact the next ranked offeror. The identified user will continue and proceed as above until one offeror indicates that it can meet the requirement of the call-up. In other words, call-ups are made based on the “right of first refusal” basis. When the highest-ranked offeror is unable to fulfill the need, the identified user is required to document its file appropriately. The resulting call-ups are considered competitive and the competitive call-up authorities can be used. LOCATION OF WORK Pacific Biological Station, Nanaimo, British Columbia. Services will be provided at a multi-building research campus comprising laboratories, office buildings, aquaculture facilities, refrigeration systems, and associated infrastructure. STANDING OFFER PERIOD The period for issuing Call-ups and providing services against the Standing Offer is from Standing Offer issuance to the date that is five (5) years thereafter (the “Expiry Date”), inclusive. TRAVEL AND LIVING EXPENSES Canada will not pay any travel or living expenses associated with performing the Work. SECURITY REQUIREMENTS There are no security requirements associated with this solicitation of offers or the Standing Offer; however, security requirements may be applicable at the time of issuance of Call-ups. Trade Agreements This procurement is subject to the provisions of the Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA), the World Trade Organization Agreement on Government Procurement (WTO-GPA), the Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), the Canada-United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement (CUKTCA), and other applicable trade agreements.

title: Design, Installation, Maintenance and Support of Electronic Security Systems
description: Given the evolving threat environment both in Canada and internationally, NRCan is focused on strengthening the physical security posture of its facilities. This includes improving access control, surveillance, and intrusion detection capabilities to ensure personnel safety and operational continuity. NRCan operates an electronic security and surveillance system consisting of access control, video management, and intrusion detection systems deployed across multiple locations nationwide. The system is maintained through a combination of in-house IT and security resources, as well as contracted security system support and integration services. The system transitioned from legacy analog infrastructure to an IP-based architecture between 2016 and 2020, with ongoing enhancements through 2023. The current security system is built on a hybrid cloud and on-premises architecture, designed to balance cost and performance with confidentiality, integrity, and availability requirements. The system includes approximately 500 card readers and 500 cameras across more than 25 sites and is monitored through the NRCan Security Operations Control Centre (SOCC) located at 580 Booth Street in Ottawa, Ontario.

title: Civilian Armored Vehicle Manufacturers
description: Civilian Armored Vehicle Manufacturers NOTICE: The purpose of this notice is for information and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation. OVERVIEW The U.S. Department of State is conducting market research to identify qualified sources capable of providing civilian armored vehicles. This Sources Sought Notice requests information from civilian armored vehicle upfitters and manufacturers to assist in acquisition planning. NAICS Code: 336211 � Motor Vehicle Body Manufacturing Small Business Size Standard: 1,000 employees PURPOSE This Sources Sought Notice seeks to identify potential vendors that specialize in civilian armored vehicles. The Government will only accept responses from firms that perform the actual armoring work from start to finish. Responses from brokers or intermediaries will not be accepted. MANUFACTURING LOCATION REQUIREMENT All vehicle armoring work under any resultant contract shall be performed at facilities located in the United States. The resultant contract will not allow the Contractor to perform or subcontract any armoring work to facilities located in countries subject to U.S. sanctions or export control restrictions. ANTICIPATED CONTRACT DETAILS Contract Type: Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Period of Performance: One (1) year base period plus nine (9) twelve-month option periods INFORMATION REQUESTED Interested parties should provide the following information in their response: 1. Company Information a. Company name b. Company address c. Point of contact (POC) name, phone number, and email address d. DUNS number (or UEI if transitioned) 2. Small Business Status a. Indicate whether your company is a small business under NAICS code 336211 b. If applicable, list the socioeconomic category in which your company belongs (e.g., 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, WOSB) 3. SAM Registration a. Confirm that your company is registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) i. Provide SAM UEI number 4. Capability Statement (20-page maximum), focusing on your firm's ability to armor various types of passenger vehicles: a. Armoring Experience � Provide details of vehicle armoring experience in the private and/or public sectors for the previous 10 years, including: i. Types of vehicles armored; make, model, and model year going back no further than 10 years. ii. Example use cases of past vehicles armored (e.g., cargo transport, VIP protection). iii. Ballistic and blast protection levels achieved for standards such as NIJ, VPAM, STANAG, etc., and any non-standard protection requirements met. iv. Fabrication capability for opaque armor materials, and types and thicknesses of materials used in previous armored vehicles. v. Client references (if releasable). b. Contract Volume and Track Record i. Total dollar value of vehicle armoring contracts/orders performed annually over the past 3 years. ii. Largest single order (by vehicle quantity and dollar value) completed within a 12-month period. c. Manufacturing Capabilities i. Location(s) of manufacturing facility/facilities. ii. Any subcontractors used in vehicle production. iii. Production capacity in vehicles per year. iv. Current production lead time, from contract/order award to delivery, for a single vehicle and for a batch order (e.g., 10, 25, 50 vehicles). v. Surge capacity: ability to increase production temporarily to meet urgent Government requirements, and associated timelines. vi. Quality certifications (e.g., ISO, industry-specific certifications). 5. Facility Security Clearances a. Details regarding current and/or past facility security clearances (e.g., FCL level and expiration date) 6. GSA Schedule (if applicable) a. GSA Schedule number b. Period of performance 7. Acquisition Strategy and Contract Structure Feedback a. Does your firm have experience performing under an IDIQ contract with multiple 12-month option periods? If so, please describe. b. Would your firm be able to compete effectively if this requirement is set aside for small business, 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, or WOSB concerns? Please explain any concerns with a small business set-aside. c. Based on your knowledge of the industry, are you aware of at least two other capable, responsible small businesses that could perform this requirement? (This helps the Government assess set-aside feasibility under the Rule of Two.) d. Would your firm prefer or recommend a single-award IDIQ or a multiple-award IDIQ for this requirement? Please explain the rationale. e. Do you have experience with, or a preference for, Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) task/delivery orders versus other pricing arrangements (e.g., FFP with economic price adjustment) for this type of work, given potential material cost volatility (e.g., steel, ballistic glass, composites)? f. What is a reasonable Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) cost range per vehicle for common armoring configurations (e.g., B4/B6 level sedan, B7 level SUV), if you are able to share this for planning purposes? g. Are there minimum order quantities or dollar thresholds your firm would require to make individual task orders economically viable? h. What is your firm's standard warranty period and terms for armoring work performed, including coverage for parts, labor, and any workmanship defects? i. Is your firm capable of providing warranty support at U.S. Department of State posts located overseas? If so, please describe how this support would be delivered, including: Delivery method � e.g., dispatch of traveling technicians from the U.S. or a regional hub, use of vetted local subcontractors/service partners, or a combination of both; Coordination with post � how your firm would coordinate with the post's General Services Office (GSO) or Facilities Management team to schedule access, obtain necessary country clearances, and comply with local security and customs requirements; Response times � anticipated timeframes for initial response and on-site arrival, accounting for post location (e.g., high-threat vs. standard posts) and regional logistics; Parts and logistics � how replacement parts or materials would be sourced and shipped to the post, including any customs, or import/export control considerations; and Limitations � any posts, regions, or security environments where your firm would be unable to provide direct warranty service, and what alternative arrangements (e.g., remote technical support, depot-level repair) would apply in those cases. j. Does your firm have bonding capacity sufficient to support a multi-year IDIQ of this size? If comfortable sharing, please indicate your bonding capacity or capacity range. k. Would your firm be interested in, or already positioned for, teaming or subcontracting arrangements with other firms to meet the full scope of this requirement? l. Are there any customer-furnished vehicle chassis considerations (e.g., Government-furnished base vehicles vs. contractor-procured) that would affect your proposed approach or pricing? m. Do you foresee any barriers (e.g., export control licensing, material sourcing, facility capacity) that could limit competition or timely performance under this requirement? SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS Deadline: Responses must be received no later than 11:00 AM EST on October 13, 2026. Submission Method: All responses, including attachments and any questions regarding this Notice, should be submitted electronically to: Maria Anguiano: anguianom@state.gov Wanda I. Cruz: cruzwi@state.gov Subject Line: Sources Sought Response � Motor Vehicle Body Manufacturing

title: Procurement Team Training
description: REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS – PROCUREMENT TEAM TRAINING    ABOUT FCC    FCC is proud to be 100% invested in Canadian agriculture and food. Our employees are committed to the long-standing success of those who produce and process Canadian food. FCC provides flexible financing and capital solutions, while creating value through data, knowledge, relationships and expertise. FCC offers a complement of financial and non-financial products and services designed to support the complex and evolving needs of the industry. As a commercial Crown corporation, FCC is a stable partner that reinvests profits back into the industry and communities it serves. For more information, visit fcc.ca.    RFP CONTACT    Farid Sokolovic  Procurement Manager  Farm Credit Canada   procurement@fcc.ca    RFP SCOPE    FCC's Strategic Sourcing Team is seeking a comprehensive Strategic Sourcing capability development program designed to elevate the team's strategic sourcing maturity and enhance procurement outcomes across the organization. The objective is to provide a customized learning experience that develops practical, end-to-end Strategic Sourcing capabilities while supporting employees with varying levels of experience and expertise.  For further details, refer to the RFP and Appendix A (RFP Schedule, Evaluation Process, Scope and Proposal Instructions) documents that are uploaded to MERX.    RFP PARTICULARS    All conditions for Proponent participation are included in the RFP documents.    RFP SCHEDULE    RFP Release Date: September 15, 2026  Proponent Questions Accepted Until:  September 29, 2026 at 2:00PM*  FCC Response to Proponent Questions Delivered Before: October 6, 2026 at 5:00PM*  RFP Closing Date/Time: October 13, 2026 at 2:00PM*    NOTE: All times are CST – Saskatchewan. The above dates are subject to change at the sole discretion of FCC. Any changes to the RFP Schedule will be communicated to all Proponents via amendment on MERX.     RFP PROCESS CONSIDERATIONS    This opportunity is covered under the provisions of Chapter 5 (Government Procurement) of the Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA) and Chapter 19 (Government Procurement) of the Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA).  FCC is subject to the Official Languages Act (Canada). Proponents may choose to respond to this RFP in their official language of choice (English or French).  This opportunity notice references a non-binding, competitive RFP, and is not a call for tenders. FCC is not obligated to proceed with the Work described in the RFP Scope, and may cancel the RFP at any time. FCC’s procurement process allows for consecutive or concurrent negotiations between FCC and one (1) or multiple Proponents, prior to awarding a Contract.    MERX ELECTRONIC BIDDING SYSTEM    This Request for Proposals (RFP), including any attachments and amendments to such RFP, is available for download by the Proponent on MERX. MERX is a Canadian Public Tenders electronic bidding system accessible at https://www.merx.com. It is the sole responsibility of the Proponent to ensure its compatibility with MERX.  Proponent proposals MUST be submitted electronically through MERX, preferably in a PDF or MS Word file, prior to the RFP Closing Date/Time specified in the RFP. Proposals submitted in other formats, by other methods or through any other means, or after the RFP Closing Date/Time specified in the RFP, may be rejected by FCC.      PRIORITY OF DOCUMENTS    In the event there are any discrepancies between this opportunity notice and the information on the MERX website proper, this opportunity notice shall take precedence.   Bidding and Documents are available on http://www.merx.com. title: Ireland – Radioactive-, toxic-, medical- and hazardous waste services – Collection and Disposal of Category 1 Waste from Dublin Airport Passenger Terminals and Airside Stables
description: Due to the risk of introducing diseases into the European Union (EU) from third countries, there are strict rules and regulations around animal products and plants and plant products entering the EU. Any products that are prohibited from entry are seized and disposed of as Category 1 waste. Prohibited products in passengers’ luggage on airplanes poses a very particular risk to public, animal and plant health, resulting in its disposal being strictly regulated. Accordingly, there are controls are in place to ensure that seizures of prohibited food or plants at Dublin Airport is controlled and disposed of in a manner that minimises risk to public, animal and plant health. Past outbreaks of diseases (e.g. Foot and Mouth Disease) demonstrate the risks posed by products of animal origin, animal by-products (ABP) and plants being introduced to Ireland through travel. The successful tenderer will be responsible for the removal, emptying, cleaning and disinfection of the Department of Agriculture, Food and Marine bins at following locations in Dublin Airport: • Terminal One • Terminal Two • Airside Stables It must be noted the successful tenderer must be registered to land Category 1 waste under Article 23 of Regulation (EC) 1069/2009 and must be registered prior to commencing operations. The operator must also ensure to abide by all relevant requirements set out in national (SI 187 2014) and EU Legislation (Regulations 1069/2009 and 142/2011). Full details in Notice titled CN25ALander, published with the tender documents. Also please note there are Terms and Conditions from Dublin Airport Authority that the successful tenderer must comply with to operate at the airport, please refer to "Dublin Airport Authority miscellaneous charges booklet 2026" published with the tender documents.

title: Trade and Cargo Academy
description: **Note: The sources sought originally posted as W912HP27RA001 - Due to technical issues with ACWS a new solicitation number was pulled. The United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Charleston District (SAC) has a new requirement for construction of a Trade and Cargo Academy at the Federal Law Enforcement Training Center (FLETC). The requirement will include hazardous material abatement and selective demolition of the current vacant 30,000 SF, three-story building, while preserving the existing main lobby and ensuring uninterrupted utility service to the occupied east wing. In its place, a new 28,400 SF, two-story, flood-resilient facility will be constructed. Due to poor soil quality and its location within FEMA Zone AE, the TCA will use a deep precast concrete pile foundation with pile-supported slabs, a heavy-duty steel frame to withstand high wind/seismic demands, a modern rainscreen envelope, and fully integrated building systems (HVAC, LED lighting, and security infrastructure). The interior will have space for instructional use on the first floor (including classrooms, an auditorium, and production spaces) and administrative open offices on the second floor. FLETC also has a requirement for the construction of a new Cargo Security and Seized Property Training Facility (CSSPTF), a separate one-story 5,985 SF facility purpose-built to support U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) training. Specifically designed for hands-on vehicle/cargo inspection, evidence processing, and simulated seized property storage, this site-adapted facility will also be elevated on a deep pile foundation to comply with stringent floodplain requirements. A key engineering focus for this site is the implementation of pile-supported stormwater piping under paved areas to mitigate soil settlement risks. Both facilities are engineered for a minimum 40-year operational lifespan, integrating highly durable, low-maintenance coastal materials, and will comply fully with the latest federal energy conservation standards, DHS security criteria, and 2021 building codes. These facilities are essential for the increased student enrollment and additional courses offered supporting FLETC Charleston.

title: Technical Services
description: This Special Notice is to advise interested members of the Training and Readiness Accelerator II (TReX 11), as well as other interested members within the U.S. technology base, that a Request for Solutions (RFS) has been issued by Advanced Technology International (ATI) for Future Training Directorate (FTD) The purpose of the Training and Readiness Accelerator II (TReX II} is to spur innovative development, demonstration, and expedited delivery of prototypes to increase Warfighter readiness via modeling, simulation, education/training, experimental validation, and military readiness focused projects. A consortium has been established to develop prototypes directly relevant to enhancing the mission effectiveness of military personnel and the supporting platforms, systems, components, or materials proposed to be acquired or developed by the Department of Defense (DOD), or to improvement of platforms, systems, components, or materials in use by the Armed Forces. Link for TREX Il-https://www.trexii.org/ This prototype project will enhance the mission effectiveness of military personnel by improving the platforms, business systems and business procedures within the Future Training Directorate (FTD). The contractor shall collect, analyze, and archive data that will support programmatic, business initiative requirements, develop and maintain related study databases and/or websites formatted for multiple toolsets, including scenario laydowns and system representations utilized within analytic tools for participation in joint experimentation, initiatives and other analysis forums. The contractor shall support the Government by assisting and performing integrated analysis, evaluations and/or assessments of organizational structures, missions, architectures with relevant analysis to include for prototyping, modeling and simulation, concepts for the realm of the possible, services, products, systems, and technologies in the areas of doctrine, organization, training, materiel, leadership and education, personnel, facilities, and policy (DOTMLPF-P).

title: Request for Information: Enterprise Training Infrastructure Project Scope Study and Feasibility Analysis
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) The Office of Acquisition Management (OAM), on behalf of the Office of the Chief Administrative Officer (OCAO), is requesting information from qualified Architectural & Engineering (A/E) firms regarding a potential business opportunity supporting future United States Capitol Police (USCP) enterprise training infrastructure planning. The United States Capitol Police recently completed a Training Facilities Requirements Assessment (TFRA) which evaluated the Department's current enterprise training infrastructure and identified operational capacity, throughput, concurrency, facility condition, and infrastructure limitations affecting the Department's ability to sustain current and future training requirements. Building upon the findings of the TFRA, USCP is seeking a qualified Architectural & Engineering (A/E) firm to conduct an Enterprise Training Infrastructure Project Scope Study and Feasibility Analysis. The purpose of the study is to further evaluate the validated operational requirements identified within the TFRA and develop feasible infrastructure alternatives capable of supporting the Department's current and future enterprise training mission. The study is expected to evaluate multiple infrastructure strategies that may include modernization or expansion of existing facilities, construction of new facilities, acquisition or leasing of facilities, utilization of partner agency resources, relocation of selected training functions, and hybrid approaches incorporating multiple infrastructure solutions. The resulting study will provide executive leadership with engineering, planning, operational, and financial information necessary to objectively evaluate infrastructure alternatives and formulate a preferred path forward balancing operational requirements, implementation realities, fiscal considerations, and future enterprise training demand. Please see the attached Statement of Objectives (SOO) for additional information regarding the proposed requirement. Submission Details Please submit the following documents to Linh.Williams@uscp.gov : Vendor Capability Statement addressing the attached Statement of Objectives (SOO). Description of the firm's experience conducting comparable Architectural & Engineering feasibility studies, infrastructure planning efforts, campus planning initiatives, or comparable federal, military, law enforcement, or public safety facility planning projects. A recommended technical approach for accomplishing the objectives identified within the SOO. A recommended scope of services, anticipated deliverables, multidisciplinary team composition, and recommended Period of Performance (POP). A Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) budgetary estimate for the proposed effort. OAM is also interested in any recommendations vendors may have to improve the proposed requirement, study methodology, acquisition strategy, or future Statement of Work. Questions & Answers Please submit all questions in writing to Linh.Williams@uscp.gov using the Attachment B - Questions and Answers Template. USCP responses to contractors' questions will be provided as an attachment to this RFI notice and amended throughout the open period of this posting, as needed. It is the responsibility of the contractor to check this posting for updates. Terms of this Request The purpose of this Request for Information (RFI) is to collect additional information regarding the subject requirement and identify the willingness and capabilities of potential vendors to support the proposed effort. This RFI is issued solely for information or planning purposes and does not constitute a Request for Quote (RFQ). The information provided in this RFI is subject to change and is not binding on the Government. USCP has not made a commitment to procure the services discussed herein, and release of this RFI should not be construed as a commitment or authorization to incur costs for which reimbursement would be required or sought. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. The USCP does not have authority to enter into contracts for architecture and engineering services or construction. The responses obtained from this RFI and any subsequent solicitation will be used to inform decision makers and stakeholders in Congress, the Legislative Branch, and partner agencies.

THIS SOLICITATION INCLUDES CMMC LEVEL 1 (SELF) REQUIREMENTS IN ACCORDANCE WITH DFARS 252.204-7025 (DEVIATION 2026-0038) AND 252.204-7021 (DEVIATION 2026-0038). This project is considered a �Large-scale Construction Project� as defined in FAR 22.502 (DEVIATION 2026-O0040). Accordingly, the requirements of FAR Subpart 22.5 (DEVIATION 2026-O0040) will apply. The Offeror shall submit a signed Project Labor Agreement with their Price Proposal submission, in accordance with FAR Provision 52.222-33 (DEVIATION 2026-O0038) and FAR Clause 52.222-34 (DEVIATION 2026-O0038). Description of Work: This design-bid-build project will include the construction of a multi-story steel frame 12,920 SF laboratory and office facility. The facility will support a variety of functions including depot level testing of critical torpedo systems. Construction consists of a steel frame building with a shallow foundation, metal standing seam roof and masonry and metal panel exterior walls. The project includes all pertinent site preparations and site improvements, including underground stormwater retention system, mechanical and electrical utilities, telecommunications, landscaping, drainage, parking and exterior lighting. For Option 1, P1016 Consolidated RDT&E Systems Facility, this project will include the construction of a multi-story 17,978 SF laboratory facility supported by shallow foundations. The facility will utilize structural steel framing with a standing-seam roof. Exteriors are planned as a combination of masonry veneer and metal panel siding. Demolition includes removal of Building 1272T, a 548 m2 engineering facility.

title: P084 NEXT GENERATION TORPEDO INTEGRATION LAB, NAVAL STATION NEWPORT, NEWPORT RI
description: Project Title/Location: DESIGN-BID-BUILD P084 NEXT GENERATION TORPEDO INTEGRATION LAB, NAVAL STATION NEWPORT, NEWPORT RI SOLICITATION NO. N4008526R0178 This acquisition is being solicited on an unrestricted basis with full and open competition. THIS SOLICITATION INCLUDES CMMC LEVEL 1 (SELF) REQUIREMENTS IN ACCORDANCE WITH DFARS 252.204-7025 (DEVIATION 2026-0038) AND 252.204-7021 (DEVIATION 2026-0038). This project is considered a �Large-scale Construction Project� as defined in FAR 22.502 (DEVIATION 2026-O0040). Accordingly, the requirements of FAR Subpart 22.5 (DEVIATION 2026-O0040) will apply. The Offeror shall submit a signed Project Labor Agreement with their Price Proposal submission, in accordance with FAR Provision 52.222-33 (DEVIATION 2026-O0038) and FAR Clause 52.222-34 (DEVIATION 2026-O0038). Offerors that do not include a signed Project Labor Agreement complying with the terms of FAR 52.222-33 (DEVIATION 2026-O0038) and 52.222-34 (DEVIATION 2026-O0038) shall be considered nonresponsive and ineligible for award. All correspondence regarding this solicitation shall be directed via email to Demetrice Jenkins at demetrice.jenkins2.civ@us.navy.mil. Description of Work: This design-bid-build project will include the construction of a multi-story steel frame 12,920 SF laboratory and office facility. The facility will support a variety of functions including depot level testing of critical torpedo systems. Construction consists of a steel frame building with a shallow foundation, metal standing seam roof and masonry and metal panel exterior walls. The project includes all pertinent site preparations and site improvements, including underground stormwater retention system, mechanical and electrical utilities, telecommunications, landscaping, drainage, parking and exterior lighting. For Option 1, P1016 Consolidated RDT&E Systems Facility, this project will include the construction of a multi-story 17,978 SF laboratory facility supported by shallow foundations. The facility will utilize structural steel framing with a standing-seam roof. Exteriors are planned as a combination of masonry veneer and metal panel siding. Demolition includes removal of Building 1272T, a 548 m2 engineering facility.

title: Request for Information: Enterprise Training Infrastructure Project Scope Study and Feasibility Analysis
description: 08/28/2026 Update: The attachment titled, "Amend 0001 Attachment B - Questions and Answers" provides the Government's responses to contractors' questions. REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) The Office of Acquisition Management (OAM), on behalf of the Office of the Chief Administrative Officer (OCAO), is requesting information from qualified Architectural & Engineering (A/E) firms regarding a potential business opportunity supporting future United States Capitol Police (USCP) enterprise training infrastructure planning. The United States Capitol Police recently completed a Training Facilities Requirements Assessment (TFRA) which evaluated the Department's current enterprise training infrastructure and identified operational capacity, throughput, concurrency, facility condition, and infrastructure limitations affecting the Department's ability to sustain current and future training requirements. Building upon the findings of the TFRA, USCP is seeking a qualified Architectural & Engineering (A/E) firm to conduct an Enterprise Training Infrastructure Project Scope Study and Feasibility Analysis. The purpose of the study is to further evaluate the validated operational requirements identified within the TFRA and develop feasible infrastructure alternatives capable of supporting the Department's current and future enterprise training mission. The study is expected to evaluate multiple infrastructure strategies that may include modernization or expansion of existing facilities, construction of new facilities, acquisition or leasing of facilities, utilization of partner agency resources, relocation of selected training functions, and hybrid approaches incorporating multiple infrastructure solutions. The resulting study will provide executive leadership with engineering, planning, operational, and financial information necessary to objectively evaluate infrastructure alternatives and formulate a preferred path forward balancing operational requirements, implementation realities, fiscal considerations, and future enterprise training demand. Please see the attached Statement of Objectives (SOO) for additional information regarding the proposed requirement. Submission Details Please submit the following documents to Linh.Williams@uscp.gov : Vendor Capability Statement addressing the attached Statement of Objectives (SOO). Description of the firm's experience conducting comparable Architectural & Engineering feasibility studies, infrastructure planning efforts, campus planning initiatives, or comparable federal, military, law enforcement, or public safety facility planning projects. A recommended technical approach for accomplishing the objectives identified within the SOO. A recommended scope of services, anticipated deliverables, multidisciplinary team composition, and recommended Period of Performance (POP). A Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) budgetary estimate for the proposed effort. OAM is also interested in any recommendations vendors may have to improve the proposed requirement, study methodology, acquisition strategy, or future Statement of Work. Questions & Answers Please submit all questions in writing to Linh.Williams@uscp.gov using the Attachment B - Questions and Answers Template. USCP responses to contractors' questions will be provided as an attachment to this RFI notice and amended throughout the open period of this posting, as needed. It is the responsibility of the contractor to check this posting for updates. Terms of this Request The purpose of this Request for Information (RFI) is to collect additional information regarding the subject requirement and identify the willingness and capabilities of potential vendors to support the proposed effort. This RFI is issued solely for information or planning purposes and does not constitute a Request for Quote (RFQ). The information provided in this RFI is subject to change and is not binding on the Government. USCP has not made a commitment to procure the services discussed herein, and release of this RFI should not be construed as a commitment or authorization to incur costs for which reimbursement would be required or sought. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. The USCP does not have authority to enter into contracts for architecture and engineering services or construction. The responses obtained from this RFI and any subsequent solicitation will be used to inform decision makers and stakeholders in Congress, the Legislative Branch, and partner agencies.

This project is considered a �Large-scale Construction Project� as defined in FAR 22.502 (DEVIATION 2026-O0040). Accordingly, the requirements of FAR Subpart 22.5 (DEVIATION 2026-O0040) will apply. The Offeror shall submit a signed Project Labor Agreement with their Price Proposal submission, in accordance with FAR Provision 52.222-33 (DEVIATION 2026-O0038) and FAR Clause 52.222-34 (DEVIATION 2026-O0038). Description of Work: This design-bid-build project will include the construction of a multi-story steel frame 12,920 SF laboratory and office facility. The facility will support a variety of functions including depot level testing of critical torpedo systems. Construction consists of a steel frame building with a shallow foundation, metal standing seam roof and masonry and metal panel exterior walls. The project includes all pertinent site preparations and site improvements, including underground stormwater retention system, mechanical and electrical utilities, telecommunications, landscaping, drainage, parking and exterior lighting. For Option 1, P1016 Consolidated RDT&E Systems Facility, this project will include the construction of a multi-story 17,978 SF laboratory facility supported by shallow foundations. Demolition includes removal of Building 1272T, a 548 m2 engineering facility.

title: Coordinated SECREP Management and Strategic Logistics Services (CSM_SLS)
description: MARCORLOGCOM provides globally responsive ground equipment inventory control and integrated operational-level logistics capabilities in order to maximize Marine Corps materiel readiness and sustainment. As part of this mission, the Marine Forces Storage Command (MFSC) CSM Program provides logistical augmentation to the Marine Corps Reparable Issue Point(s) (RIP) located at I, II, and III MEF, as well as MFR in support of the CSM program, which is detailed in MCO 4400.200A. Additionally, the MFSC CSM Program performs strategic level CPI in consonance with the Logistics Modernization Solution Initiating Directive (LSMID) that outlines anticipated Realignment of Supply (ROS) outcomes for SECREP management. Finally, the MFSC CSM Program performs strategic level supply chain management, coordinated retail management, and logistics services planning for the Marine Corps, which makes up the Strategic Logistics Services (SLS) portion of this requirement. This is a small business set-aside for SeaPort-NxG MAC holders.

title: Mobile & Data Services for the U.S. Embassy Panama

The Embassy intends to conduct a pre-quotation conference, and all prospective quoters are invited to attend. Quotations are due by 3:00p.m. on Tuesday, October 13th, 2026. No quotations will be accepted after this time. Quotations must be in English and incomplete quotations will not be accepted. Your quotation must be submitted electronically to PNMPROCREQ@state.gov . It is important to make sure the submission is made in specific size and format; in MS-Word 2007/2010 or MS-Excel 2007/2010 or Adobe Acrobat (pdf) file format. The file size must not exceed 30MB. If the file size should exceed the 30MB, the submission must be made in separate files and attached to separate emails with less than 30MB each. When notifying the Contracting Officer of the reasons for making substitutions, the type of change shall be indicated by code number in accordance with one of the following statements: Code 1: PART NUMBER CHANGE/MINOR DESIGN CHANGE - If the Manufacturer's Part Number or item design indicated thereon has changed, but form, fit and function of the item is not affected thereby, and the design change meets the criteria for minor, by not effecting form, fit, function, reliability or safety , supply the item and advise SPCC immediately of the new part number, furnishing a detail drawing and/or a detailed description of the change, as applicable. Code 2: Assembly (or set or kit) not furnished - Used following detail parts. Code 3: Part not furnished separately - Use assembly. Code 4: Part redesigned - Old and new parts are completely interchangeable. Code 5: Part redesigned - New part replaces old. Old part cannot replace new. Code 6: Part redesigned - Parts not interchangeable. 3.4 Mercury Free - The material supplied under this contract/purchase order is intended for use on submarines/surface ships and therefore shall contain no metallic mercury and shall be free from mercury contamination. Mercury contamination of the material will be cause for rejection. If the inclusion of metallic mercury is required as a functional part of the material furnished under this contract, the Contractor shall obtain written approval from the Procurement Contracting Officer before proceeding with manufacture. The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. Such a request will be forwarded directly to the Procurement Contracting Officer with a copy to the applicable Government Inspector. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. These requirements shall be included in any subcontract or purchase order hereunder and the Contractor shall insure SubContractor compliance with these requirements. Technical questions pertaining to these requirements shall be referred to the Procurement Contracting Officer via the cognizant Administrative Contracting Officer. For background, the following information is provided: Mercury is corrosive to gold, silver, nickel, stainless steels, aluminum and copper alloys. Stainless steels, nickel, and copper alloys are widely used in reactor plants and other submarine/surface ship systems. Accidental trapping of mercury in a component could cause serious damage to vital parts. Mercury is also toxic if inhaled, ingested, or absorbed through the skin. It is evident that grave consequences could result from small amounts of mercury vapor present in an unreplenished submarine/surface ship atmosphere. 4. QUALITY ASSURANCE 4.1 Responsibil

PROCEDURES:The contractor shall prepare and maintain Quality Control Documentation, test and repair procedures, and inspection procedures which shall be made available to the Government for review and approval. The procedures shall include sequential diagrams of the test, repair, and inspection process, as well as the performance spcifications to perform the procedures. QUALITY ASSURANCE PROGRAM PLAN: The contractor shall develop, implement and maintain a Repair Quality Plan in compliance with the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q-9858, ISO,9000 / 9001 / 9002, or equvalent.The plan shall define the specific methods by which compliance with contractual requirements will be assured. A parts control system shall establish a record of performance for each purchased and internally manufactured part and shall be used to evaluate continued use of the source. Evidence of such inspections shall be maintained for Government review at least twelve (12) months following acceptance of the end item. Inspection reports shall be maintained by the contractor. The inspection report shall, at a minimum, include a record of all dimensional data (coordinate/positional), material, finish, and process with appropriate pass/fail criteria, such ascertifications, and actual dimensional readings. FAILURE ANALYSIS AND CORRECTIVE ACTION:All failure analysis and corrective action reports/plans shall be submitted to the Government. NONCONFORMING MATERIAL:The contractor shall establish an effective system for controlling nonconforming material including procedures for identification, segregation, and disposition. A complete file of IRB actions shall be maintained for review by the Government for concurrance of classification. MATERIAL REVIEW BOARD (MRB):Formal MRB authority for disposition of "AS-IS"and for minor non-conformances is retained by the Government. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. These requirements shall be included in any subcontract or purchase order hereunder and the Contractor shall insure SubContractor compliance with these requirements. Technical questions pertaining to these requirements shall be referred to the Procurement Contracting Officer via the cognizant Administrative Contracting Officer. For background, the following information is provided: Mercury is corrosive to gold, silver, nickel, stainless steels, aluminum and copper alloys. Stainless steels, nickel, and copper alloys are widely used in reactor plants and other submarine/surface ship systems. Accidental trapping of mercury in a component could cause serious damage to vital parts. Mercury is also toxic if inhaled, ingested, or absorbed through the skin.
